items.followUp: Describe how Group-I metals react with water.

rubric.why: Identifies the general product formed when Group-I metals react with oxygen.
rubric.description: States that Group-I metals react with oxygen to form oxides.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reaction forms oxides.

rubric.why: A balanced example equation demonstrates the reaction.
rubric.description: Gives a correctly balanced example of a Group-I metal reacting with oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct balanced example equation.

modelAnswer: Group-I metals react with oxygen to form oxides.

items.followUp: Write the formula of aluminium oxide using the valencies of aluminium and oxygen.

rubric.why: The symbols and valencies are the starting information for writing the formula.
rubric.description: Writes the symbols and valencies of the elements or ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Al³⁺ and O²⁻.

rubric.why: The positive component is written before the negative component in the formula.
rubric.description: Writes the positive symbol first and the negative symbol second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct order of the symbols.

rubric.why: Crossing the valencies gives the formula subscripts.
rubric.description: Crosses the valencies to become subscripts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for applying the criss-cross method.

rubric.why: Formula subscripts must give the simplest whole-number ratio.
rubric.description: Reduces the subscripts to the simplest whole-number ratio when necessary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or demonstrating reduction to the simplest ratio.

rubric.why: The correct formula is the final result of the worked example.
rubric.description: Gives the formula of aluminium oxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula Al₂O₃.

modelAnswer: Write the symbols of the elements or ions and note their valencies: Al³⁺ and O²⁻.
Write the positive symbol first and the negative symbol second: Al O.
Cross the valencies to become subscripts: Al₂O₃.
Reduce the subscripts to the simplest whole-number ratio if necessary; here they cannot be reduced.
Therefore, the formula of aluminium oxide is Al₂O₃.

items.followUp: Write four properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles.
rubric.description: States that canal rays consist of positive ions or positively charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the particles as positively charged.

rubric.why: Straight-line travel is a characteristic property of canal rays.
rubric.description: States that canal rays travel in straight lines.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the straight-line property.

rubric.why: Their deflection in fields is a property of canal rays and demonstrates their charge.
rubric.description: States that canal rays are deflected by electric or magnetic fields, or toward the negative plate in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct statement about field deflection or its direction.

rubric.why: Canal-ray particles originate from the gas in the discharge tube, so their properties vary with the gas.
rubric.description: States that the nature or charge-to-mass ratio of canal-ray particles depends on the gas used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles or their properties depend on the gas.

modelAnswer: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles (positive ions).
They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields; in an electric field they move toward the negative plate.
Their particles depend on the gas present in the discharge tube, so their mass and charge-to-mass ratio can vary.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a physical change and a chemical change.

rubric.why: A physical property can be observed or measured without altering chemical identity.
rubric.description: Defines physical properties as observable or measurable without changing a substance's composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that composition or chemical identity remains unchanged.

rubric.why: A chemical property describes a substance's ability to undergo a change in chemical identity.
rubric.description: Defines chemical properties as describing how a substance can form new substances or change composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a chemical change alters composition or forms a new substance.

modelAnswer: A physical property can be observed or measured without changing the chemical composition or identity of a substance.
A chemical property describes how a substance can react to form new substances, changing its chemical composition.
